title: Head of Business Change
description:
Are you an experienced transformation leader who knows how to turn ambitious strategy into change that actually lands and lasts?We’re looking for a Head of Business Change to join our Business Change team at Specsavers. This is an exciting senior leadership opportunity with a global remit, leading a team of senior change professionals and shaping how we deliver, adopt and embed change across some of our most important strategic programmes.This is much more than leading individual change programmes. You’ll take a portfolio-wide view, translating our strategic direction into an integrated change plan and ensuring we have the right priorities, capability and resources in place. You’ll oversee everything from change impact and organisational readiness through to engagement, communications, learning and adoption, making sure transformation delivers meaningful and sustainable business outcomes.You’ll also have the opportunity to shape the future of Business Change at Specsavers. Leading a team of 10–15 direct and indirect reports, you’ll continue to mature our change capability, developing globally consistent standards, methodologies and ways of working while exploring how innovative approaches, technology and AI can make change more effective. You’ll lead through other senior leaders, develop future talent and create a high-performing culture built around collaboration, accountability and continuous improvement.We’re looking for someone with significant senior leadership experience across business change or enterprise transformation, with a proven track record of leading complex, multi-programme change in a global organisation. You’ll bring strong knowledge of organisational readiness, adoption and benefits realisation, alongside the commercial judgement and strategic thinking needed to prioritise activity and make informed decisions in a complex environment.Just as importantly, you’ll be a highly credible and influential leader. You’ll build trusted relationships across regional, functional and global leadership teams, using insight, evidence and compelling storytelling to challenge thinking, influence strategic decisions and ensure our organisation is genuinely ready for change.If you’re excited by the opportunity to lead a global change capability, develop an outstanding team and play a major part in delivering Specsavers’ long-term transformation ambitions, we’d love to hear from you.Join us as Head of Business Change and help turn our biggest ambitions into lasting change

title: Executive Director of Operations - Remote with Travel
description:
At FitzRoy, we believe everyone deserves to live a gloriously ordinary life, filled with purpose, choice and happiness. For over 60 years, we've been supporting people with learning disabilities, autism, mental health needs and forensic backgrounds to live the lives they choose. Today, our services span residential care, supported living and community-based support across England. But we're not standing still. As we shape our ambitious strategy for 2027 and beyond, we're looking for an exceptional Executive Director of Operations to help lead our next chapter.This is an opportunity to influence the future of an established, values-led charity, bringing together outstanding operational leadership, strategic thinking and the creativity to challenge how things have always been done.The opportunityWe're looking for someone who understands social care from the inside out. Someone who knows what it takes to run great services, has the credibility to guide and challenge experienced operational leaders, and can also step confidently into the boardroom, influence senior stakeholders and help shape organisational strategy.You'll lead our regional operations, creating a culture of accountability, visible leadership and continuous improvement. You'll ensure that our services are safe, effective and sustainable, while empowering your leadership team to deliver exceptional outcomes for the people we support.But this role is about much more than overseeing today's operations. You'll help us anticipate what's next for adult social care, navigate an increasingly complex political and commissioning environment, and explore new opportunities to innovate, diversify and grow.Working alongside dedicated Quality and Business Development functions, you'll bring the operational expertise, commercial judgement and fresh thinking needed to turn ambitious ideas into successful, sustainable services.What makes this opportunity different?We're entering an exciting period of change, with a strategy being built around three key ambitions that you'll have a genuine opportunity to shape how these ambitions become reality, influencing not only how we deliver services today, but what FitzRoy looks like in the years ahead.About youYou'll be an accomplished senior leader with substantial experience in regulated adult social care, particularly supporting people with learning disabilities and autism.You'll bring:Deep operational credibility – a strong understanding of frontline services, combined with proven experience leading complex, geographically dispersed operations.Exceptional leadership – the ability to inspire, develop and challenge senior managers, creating accountability and delivering results through others.Strategic vision and political awareness – the confidence to influence at Board level, anticipate sector developments and navigate complex commissioning and stakeholder relationships.Commercial acumen and creativity – the ability to identify opportunities, challenge conventional thinking and help develop innovative, sustainable models of support.Strong professional judgement – extensive knowledge of CQC regulation, safeguarding and operational risk, with the ability to identify issues early and drive meaningful improvement.A visible, values-led approach – someone who connects with people, listens, leads with integrity and never loses sight of the individuals behind the services.Above all, we're looking for someone who can combine strategic ambition with genuine operational understanding. A leader who is as comfortable engaging with people in our services as they are influencing commissioners, presenting to Trustees or shaping our future strategy.Why FitzRoy?Because this is an opportunity to make a difference on a significant scale, in an organisation where purpose and values genuinely matter.You'll join a committed Executive Leadership Team, work with talented colleagues across the organisation and have the scope to bring new ideas, challenge established thinking and help shape our future.We're proud of what FitzRoy has achieved, but we're equally excited about what comes next.BenefitsSalary up to £90,000 per annum DOE30 days holiday rising to 35 with 5 years service, plus bank holidays.£6,000 car allowance. Private medical Insurance. Healthcare cash plan.  EV salary sacrifice scheme. Pension and Life Assurance.About UsFitzRoy is a national charity, set up 60 years ago by brave parents as a pioneering alternative to institutional care. Their values remain the values of FitzRoy today – we see the person, we are brave and we are creative – and they thread through everything we do.We support hundreds of people with a range of needs. You could be supporting someone with learning disabilities, autism, acquired brain injuries or mental health support needs. Many of the people we support also have physical impairments or other health issues. Working for us will give you an opportunity to learn, to grow and to transform lives. Join us today.

description:
Job SummaryThe Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social, and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution, and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime, and migration.This role is within the Advanced Data Formats Service in Digital Publishing, which aims to support users to find, understand, explore and use ONS data. We look after and improve the services that make data available through the ONS website, downloads, interactive tools and APIs, while developing better ways for people and machines to access trusted statistics. Our work brings together data, technology and user needs, replacing older services with simpler, more joined-up ways to publish and use ONS data.Job DescriptionA delivery manager will build and maintain teams, ensuring they are motivated, collaborating and working well. The complexity or breadth of products or teams will vary in this role, depending on the context.They Also:Identify obstacles and help the team to overcome them.Focus the team on what is most important to the delivery of products and services. Encourage and facilitate continuous improvement of the delivery team.Coach and mentor both team members and others to apply the most appropriate Agile and Lean tools and techniques. Person specificationEssential Criteria:Agile and Lean Practices (Practitioner):You Can:compare and select the most appropriate delivery methods and processesrecognise, reflect and adapt when something does not work, encouraging experimentationuse a blended approach depending on the contexthelp teams to measure, evaluate and visualise outcomesencourage reflective practice to improve ways of working You Can:Communicating between the technical and non-technical (Practitioner):listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectationsmanage active and reactive communicationsupport or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders You Can:Maintaining delivery momentum (Practitioner):Facilitate the delivery flow of a team, managing the pace and tempo.Actively address internal and external risks, issues and dependencies including where ownership exists outside the team. You Can:Making the process work (Expert):Identify and challenge organisational processes of increasing complexity and those processes that are unnecessarily complicated.Add value and can coach the organisation to inspect and adapt processes.Understand external suppliers’ delivery approaches and adapt to ensure interface to ONS delivery approach is smooth, challenging external supplier to align more closely where appropriate.Guide teams through the implementation of a new process. Life cycle management (Working)You Can:manage the delivery of products and services that add value through different phases of the life cycle, with some supportidentify if the product or service should move to the next phase and, if it should, how to do thisensure the product or service is developed in line with the appropriate service standards for a phaseuse new information to adapt approaches to life cycle managementBehavioursWe'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:Changing and ImprovingDelivering at PaceWorking TogetherCommunicating and InfluencingBenefitsAlongside your salary of £43,329, Office for National Statistics contributes £12,552 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme.  Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).The Office for National Statistics is part of the Civil Service, and as such we share a number of key benefits with other departments, whilst also having our own unique offerings to support our valued colleagues across the organisation.Whether you are hearing about us for the first time or already know a bit about our organisation, we hope that our careers site will give you a great insight into the benefits and facilities available to our colleagues, and our fantastic working culture. Inclusion & AccessibilityAt ONS we are always looking to attract the very best people from the widest possible talent pool, and we are proud to be an inclusive, equal opportunities employer. As a Disability Confident Leader we’re committed to ensuring that all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.As part of our application process, you will be prompted to provide details of any reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process that you need. If you would like to discuss any reasonable adjustments before applying, please contact the recruitment team in the first instance.If you would like an accessible version of any of the attachments or recruitment documents below or linked to in this advert, please contact the recruitment team who will be happy to assist.Things you need to knowSelection process detailsThis vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours and Experience.We are dedicated to providing equal opportunities for all, and are proud participants in the following initiatives:Disability Confident Scheme (opens in new window).Great Place to Work for Veterans (opens in a new window).Redeployment Interview Scheme (open to Civil Service employees at risk of redundancy who meet the minimum requirements)Visa SponsorshipONS is unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have a valid right to work in the UK when employment commences. If you are currently in the UK on a time-limited visa, it must have at least 18 months remaining at the point of application.Right To Work And Nationality RequirementsTo work at ONS, applicants must meet the Civil Service nationality requirements, satisfy UK right to work requirements and, where applicable, meet the relevant security clearance requirements.If you are unsure whether you meet the appropriate right to work or security clearance eligibility criteria, please refer to the guidance on Gov.uk or contact the recruitment email provided in the advert before applying. Failure to meet these requirements will result in your application being rejected and employment offers being withdrawn.Application ProcessNumber of Stages: 2Stage 1: ApplicationStage 2: InterviewStage 1 – Application The assessment process at the application stage will be based on your work history, CV, skills, experience, and personal statement. It is important that your application is tailored to highlight the skills, knowledge, and experience relevant to the role.A personal statement is required at application stage, the maximum word count allowed is 1,250 words, which should not be exceeded. You should provide evidence for each essential skill criterion listed in the person specification. As these criteria are scored, it is advisable to give clear examples for each one, including the impact of your actions, ideally utilising the STAR technique (Situation, Task, Action, Result).In instances where a high number of applications are received, the sift pass mark may be adjusted, and candidates will be invited to interview based on merit order, i.e., those with the highest scores.Please note that Success Profiles Behaviour examples are not required at this stage of the application process.When a high volume of applications are received, the sift pass mark may be adjusted. Candidates will be invited to interview based on their merit order, with those achieving the highest scores being prioritised. Applicants who score below the adjusted pass mark but still pass will be placed on hold and may be invited to interview at a later date.We often have similar roles available at different grades. If a candidate is suitable for a similar role or a lower grade than they have applied for, we may offer the candidate that role without the need to go through a further selection process providing the role has the same behaviours, and essential skills.Stage 2 – InterviewInterviews will be virtual via Microsoft Teams.If invited to interview, you will be assessed using techniques aligned with the Civil Service Success Profiles framework, covering all behaviours listed in the job advert and any required technical skills.A reserve list may be held for a period up to 12 months from which further appointments may be made.Important DatesSift will be conducted from 3/12/2026Interviews will be conducted from w/c 14/12/2026For the full terms and conditions of the post, please see attachment.Please note that all campaigns may be subject to withdrawal at any stage if the internal resource position changes.Feedback will only be provided if you attend an interview or assessment.Security and legal requirementsIf successful, you must undergo a Basic (or equivalent) level of criminal record check, and complete Baseline Personnel Security Standard (opens in a new window) checks.You also must meet security requirements before you can be appointed. The clearance level needed for this role is Counter Terrorist Check (opens in a new window).Don’t worry if you aren’t used to vetting procedures. We are committed to making vetting as straightforward and as accessible as possible to all. See our vetting charter (opens in a new window) for more information.We welcome applications from a diverse range of candidates, but we have some specific requirements regarding nationality. You will be asked to confirm you are eligible under these requirements as part of the application process. You can find them in Civil Service Nationality Rules (opens in a new window).Working for the Civil ServiceIn the Civil Service, we take pride in our values and the high standards of behaviour expected of us. As a civil servant, you will be expected to act in line with the Civil Service Code (opens in a new window). Recruitment is no different, and all appointments follow the  Civil Service Commission's Recruitment Principles (opens in a new window).We are committed to attracting and developing talented people from all backgrounds, actively supporting an inclusive culture.If successful in your application, you’ll be joining both Office for National Statistics and the wider UK Civil Service (opens in a new window). This community spans a range of government departments (opens in a new window), professions and functions (opens in a new window) that serve the UK and its public.Apply and further informationArtificial intelligenceArtificial intelligence can be a useful tool to support your application, however, all examples and statements provided must be truthful, factually accurate and taken directly from your own experience. Where plagiarism has been identified (presenting the ideas and experiences of others, or generated by artificial intelligence, as your own) applications may be withdrawn and internal candidates may be subject to disciplinary action. Please see our candidate guidance (opens in a new window) for more information on appropriate and inappropriate use.Once this job has closed, the job advert will no longer be available. You may want to save a copy for your records.Contact point for applicantsJob Contact :Name : Government Digital and Data RecruitmentEmail : Government-Digital-and-Data-Recruitment@ons.gov.ukRecruitment teamEmail : about.you@ons.gov.ukFurther informationIf you feel your application has not been treated in accordance with the Recruitment Principles and you wish to make a complaint, in the first instance, you should contact recruitment.complaints@ons.gov.uk. If you are not satisfied with the response you receive from the Department, you can contact the Civil Service Commission

title: Project Manager
description:
Job DescriptionAt CMDP+ we believe that people matter. We know that to build successful, creative teams we need a diverse workforce that can deliver new innovative ways of thinking. We provide an environment where you will have the freedom to develop and grow to your full potential.CMDP+ is looking to strengthen their Delivery team with a Construction and Delivery Lead / Project Manager for our Southern Water Framework. MWH Treatment and Costain Group are part of the CMDP+ joint venture that will deliver a range of construction schemes to maintain and improve Southern Water’s water supply and wastewater treatment works within the South and Southeast regions.The Joint Venture has been set up specifically to execute the 5-year (2025 – 2030) AMP8 capital delivery framework. We will be delivering a programme of works up to £1bn over the 5-year period consisting of both heavy civil engineering and mechanical and electrical activities.At Costain, we believe diverse perspectives drive innovation. If you’re passionate about making a positive impact and think you can bring value to our team, we’d love to hear from you—even if you don’t tick every box. Your unique skills and experiences could be exactly what we need.ResponsibilitiesManagement of Client interface meetings and reporting of progress/cost to the CMDP PM and Commercial Team representative. Manage, supervise, train and mentor the site teams to enable them to optimise their work contribution. Management of H&S and Quality data with the site team for reporting purposes. Review contractual agreements and develop working methods, programme and forecast costs with the Client, Contracts Manager and Specialist / Suppliers identifying any inaccuracies or inconsistencies.Manage and undertake internal project reviews Develop programmes and forecast budgets, assess actual programme and productivity achieved and review weekly, taking action where appropriate, and reporting any changes to the Contracts Manager and Commercial department. Be fully conversant with specialists’ contract conditions. Positively manage the programme to ensure the appropriate specialists provide the level of resources with the necessary skills so as not to impede the construction programme. Communicate with the Contracts Manager, site team and the commercial team’s issues of non-conformances and contractual correspondence. Ensure that comprehensive records of resources employed on additional works are maintained. Ensure that a full and accurate daily site diary is kept, including any changes / variations, specialists’ attendance, and records of work-related discussions with the design team /site team. Ensure that inspection and test plans, risk assessments and method statements for the control of the works are reviewed, approved and adhered to. Keep abreast of developments in professional field Adherence to Costain policies and procedures Supervising responsibility for site teams; liaison with internal and external stakeholders Be familiar with, and demonstrate commitment to the requirements of the Health & Safety and Environmental Policies Management of design partner(s) in the delivery of project specifications and deliverables. Responsible for the overall delivery of contracts within your allocated portfolioQualificationsDegree level qualification in a Civil Engineering allied subject or HND in Civil Engineering and vocational training in EngineeringUnderstanding of Engineering PrinciplesKnowledge and understanding of construction contract law and forms of contract through experience and formal training.Extensive technical knowledge of construction techniques and best practices.Computer competence (MS Word, Excel, Document control system, Primavera software). Relevant CSCS CardTraining in Health & Safety and Environmental managementCurrent Driving LicenceExperience of resource management and workforce efficiencyExperience of NEC3 or 4Desirable (the ideal)Water industry experienceDegree in Civil EngineeringMICEMAPMComputer competence Vocational Training (successful experience of project management)About UsCostain helps to improve people’s lives with integrated, leading edge, smart infrastructure solutions across the UK’s energy, water, transportation and defence markets. We help our clients improve their business performance by increasing capacity, improving customer service, safeguarding security, enhancing resilience, decarbonising and delivering increased efficiency. Our vision is to be the UK’s leading smart infrastructure solutions company. We will achieve this by focusing on blue chip clients whose major spending plans are underpinned by strategic national needs, regulatory commitments, legislation or essential performance requirements. We offer our clients leading edge solutions that are digitally optimised through the following five services which cover the whole lifecycle of their assets: future-shaping strategic consultancy; consultancy and advisory; digital technology solutions; asset optimisation and complex programme delivery. Our culture and values underpin everything we do.Costain appreciate the time and effort taken when applying for one of our positions but, due to the high volume of responses, we are unable to provide individual feedback on candidates at application phase.We do share individual feedback following an interview .A Disability Confident employer will generally offer an interview to any applicant that disclose they have a disability and meets the minimum criteria for the job as defined by the employer.It is important to note that in certain recruitment situations such as high-volume, seasonal and high-peak times, the employer may wish to limit the overall numbers of interviews offered to both disabled people and non-disabled people.For more details please go to the Disability Confident website:https://www.gov.uk/government/collections/disability-confident-campaign

title: Renal Clinic Area Manager
description:
An exciting new opportunity has arisen for a committed Regional Operations Manager to provide both strategic and operational leadership to Dialysis Clinic Managers across the London South West, East, and North regions. The role requires regular travel across clinics, with approximately 60:80 of your working week spent on:site supporting services and teamsThis is an independent, nurse:led provider, working in partnership with the NHS to deliver the highest standards of dialysis care using cutting:edge technology in welcoming, modern environments**To be considered for this position you must have previous established leadership experience within a healthcare provider is essential + Experience in an outpatient haemodialysis setting would be highly advantageous**As The Regional Operations Manager Your Key Responsibilities Include Coaching and developing your team of Clinic Managers to help achieve their professional and personal goals Creating a fulfilling work environment through strategic leadership and support to teammates within clinics Driving financial and revenue growth whilst maintaining excellent clinical outcomes Managing relationships with external partners such as NHS Trusts and the CQC Understanding and analysing metrics impacting service delivery and other key factors Building great relationships with internal stakeholders throughout the business, including UK and International Head Office Implementing new processes to drive quality improvements for both patients and teammates Ensuring compliance with all relevant clinical, governance and regulatory systems and policiesThe following skills and experience would be preferred and beneficial for the role: Previous established leadership experience within a healthcare provider is essential and experience in an outpatient haemodialysis setting would be highly advantageous Demonstrable experience in planning and managing at strategic and operational level Strong business acumen; able to assess financial implications of decisions and actions Engaging communication skills and a friendly demeanour to successfully connect with a diverse team and patients Lead by example style to encourage a value driven culture that brings the best out of everyone Entrepreneurial attitude and pragmatic approach to problem solving in changing situations in a clinical environment Advanced computer skills and proficiency in MS Excel required; intermediate skills and proficiency in MS Word, Outlook, and PowerPoint requiredThe successful Regional Operations Manager will receive an excellent salary of GBP50,000 : GBP55,000 per annum. In return for your hard work and commitment you will receive the following generous benefits:**OTE Bonus of GBP5k + Company Car** Company Pension Scheme 35 days paid leave per annum, including bank holidays Life Assurance to 3 times annual salary Retail discount scheme membership ANN UK MembershipReference ID: 7290for this fantastic job role, please call on 638 or send your CV

title: Senior FICO Consultant
company: Oxoid Remel Microbiology (Acquired from Thermo Fisher Scientific)
description:
Joining our team, you'll play an active part in helping to deliver meaningful impact. At Oxoid Remel Microbiology, acquired from Thermo Fisher Scientific, we play a crucial role in accurate identification and targeted treatment for diseases, ensuring food and beverage safety, and supporting pharmaceutical manufacturing integrity. Our products and services are designed to meet the highest standards of quality and performance, helping our customers achieve their objectives efficiently and effectively.You lead the SAP FICO functional build on Oxoid Remel Microbiology's cloned SAP environments, working closely with Finance, IT, the seller and implementation partners to deliver a controlled, supportable solution by the TSA exit deadline.You provide hands-on SAP FI/CO expertise across requirements, design, configuration, data validation, testing, cutover and hypercare. You ensure the solution supports how the business needs to operate after separation.After cutover, you become Oxoid Remel Microbiology's SAP FICO lead: partnering with Finance and other business teams on SAP projects, enhancements and day-to-day support, and managing the functional backlog for the SAP finance estate.The Build You LeadOwn the FICO functional workstream — shape scope, requirements, design decisions, configuration, dependencies, risks and readiness for the cloned ECC and S/4HANA environments. Coordinate delivery with the implementation partner and keep the work focused on the TSA exit plan.Translate business needs into SAP solutions — work with Finance process owners to understand record-to-report, order-to-cash and procure-to-pay requirements; assess the cloned configuration; identify gaps; and design practical solutions for Oxoid Remel Microbiology’s standalone operating model.Lead configuration and build activity — oversee and perform FICO configuration across relevant areas such as general ledger, accounts payable, accounts receivable, asset accounting, cost centre accounting, internal orders and profitability analysis, as applicable to the agreed scope. Coordinate dependencies with other SAP modules and connected systems. Consulting on FICO aspects of Legal Entity separation in sellers SAP estate.Drive data, testing and TSA exit readiness — define and validate finance master and transactional data requirements; partner with data and technical teams on migration, integrations and reconciliation; and lead functional testing, cutover preparation, business validation and hypercare so Oxoid Remel Microbiology can operate independently as seller-provided services are withdrawn.The Functional Ownership You BringFit-for-purpose finance processes — ensure SAP configuration supports clear, workable finance processes and roles across entities. Document key decisions and processes, and help business owners understand and adopt the solution.Controlled, reconciled finance data — establish validation and reconciliation routines so that ledgers, sub-ledgers, migrated balances and connected feeds are complete, accurate and ready for close and reporting.A supportable SAP solution — maintain functional design and configuration documentation, support controls and audit requirements, and ensure the build is handed over effectively to Oxoid Remel Microbiology’s business and IT teams.After Go-Live — The SAP FICO Lead RolePartner with the business — work with Finance and other teams on SAP projects, process changes and continuous improvement. Turn business needs into clear requirements and functional solutions, and lead FICO delivery through design, testing and release.Own functional support and improvement — triage SAP FICO issues, coordinate resolution with IT and external partners, advise users, manage enhancements and maintain a clear functional backlog. Help the business improve processes, controls, automation and reporting as Oxoid Remel Microbiology evolves.What You BringStrong hands-on SAP FI/CO experience across both ECC and S/4HANA, including functional design, configuration, testing and support.Experience leading or playing a senior functional role in an SAP build, separation, carve-out, migration or transformation, ideally with a fixed TSA exit date.Practical knowledge of core finance processes and their SAP implementation, with the ability to engage confidently with finance users, IT teams and implementation partners.Experience with data migration, finance master data, integrations, reconciliation, cutover and hypercare.A collaborative, hands-on approach; able to lead workshops, clarify requirements, make sound functional decisions and manage issues through to resolution.This is an exciting time to join us as we continue to build on more than 100 years of microbiology excellence. With a broad portfolio of instruments, services, and global resources, we’re steadfast in our commitment to helping you succeed. Together, we can cultivate a thriving microbiology culture that supports you today, tomorrow, and for life. Oxoid Remel Microbiology, acquired from Thermo Fisher Scientific, is now under the ownership of Astorg, a leading private equity firm with deep healthcare sector expertise and proven track record in diagnostics. With the continuity of trusted brands, established expertise and a long-standing reputation in microbiology, we’re looking for talented people to join us as we enter our next chapter of growth. Come and be part of what’s next for our company.

title: Delivery Manager
description:
Right across infrastructure, there’s a requirement to not only maintain, but also renew and reimagine. Whatever stage you’re at in your career, with us you’ll have an opportunity to grow and develop. Delivering essential infrastructure services for life, while being safety first, and client and customer centric in a friendly, fun and respectful environment where you are encouraged to thrive.Where will you be working?We help our clients safeguard the water supply, improve environmental performance and manage demand for future generations. We enhance and extend asset life, ensuring compliance with water quality and environmental standards. We’re problem solvers with over 140 years of combined experience in engineering and infrastructure.This role will be within our Water and wastewater capital project delivery team. Our teams deliver large-scale capital programmes aimed at keeping water infrastructure resilient for the long-term while protecting the environment.Want to be a part of it?What will you be doing? As the Delivery Manager, you’ll take responsibility for commercial oversight across a portfolio of projects, making sure they are delivered efficiently, in line with contract requirements and to the standards our clients expect.This is to deliver AMP8 Infrastructure projects working on Southern Water Framework.You'll lead the successful delivery of a portfolio of infrastructure and construction projects, ensuring they are delivered safely, compliantly, on time and within budget. We'll need you to oversee programme planning, resource allocation and project performance across multiple workstreams, coordinating labour, plant and materials to maintain delivery and keep programmes on track.As part of this role, you'll be responsible for maintaining strong governance and compliance standards, ensuring accurate project reporting, forecasting and performance data, while meeting contractual, statutory and organisational requirements. Working closely with Commercial Managers, you'll drive commercial performance through effective cost control, forecasting, cashflow management and change governance, making informed decisions that protect contract value and performance.You'll build strong relationships with clients, subcontractors and internal stakeholders, providing clear updates on progress, risks and key issues while driving timely resolution of challenges. You'll proactively identify and mitigate risks, champion continuous improvement and value engineering initiatives, and apply lessons learned across projects to enhance future delivery.As the Delivery Manager, you'll lead, develop and support your team, creating the conditions for high performance, collaboration and consistent delivery while always promoting M Group's health, safety and environmental standards.What You’ll BringDo you have a degree in Engineering, Construction Management or a related discipline, or equivalent experience - This is desirable. Have you got relevant certifications such as CSCS, SMSTS and IOSH or NEBOSH?Do you hold a valid Driving Licence?Have you got experience working across multidisciplinary projects or portfolios in highways and street works environments?Are you experienced in supporting commercial assurance activities?Can you lead open, meaningful conversations about performance, development and potential?Are you able to Identify and develop future talent, supporting succession planning along with planning resources and oversee recruitment, onboarding and retention? Can you consistently demonstrate our people manager standards and actively coach others to do the same?What’s in it for you?We offer a range of benefits designed to support your life in and out of work, some of which include;Contributory pension schemeOnline GP service, 24 hours a day, 365 days a year Employee assistance programmeMy Rewards portal, access to 1000’s of retail discountsLife assuranceCycle to work, salary finance and give as you earn schemes Enhanced maternity, paternity leave and adoption leaveReward and recognition scheme Recommend a friend - get rewarded for introducing people to us!In addition, this role offers;Company car and fuel card with a range of EV and hybrid vehicles to choose fromMy Car Choice our salary sacrifice EV/ Hybrid car scheme Health Care Cash Plan, giving you and your family the ability to claim back medical expenses for things like dental, eyecare and physiotherapy and much more! Private Healthcare - family cover25 days annual leave plus bank holidays Discretionary bonus schemeAbout UsWe want to be an employer of choice and a great place to work, attracting diverse and talented people, who join us and make a difference. We’re one of the Top 100 UK companies actively supporting and recruiting veterans. Our ENABLE inclusion networks bring together people who have a shared passion, to help create an environment where everyone belongs.Our values help to shape our culture and how we work with one another. We recruit with these values in mind, to ensure your aspirations, and ways of working, align with ours.We’re responsible and go further for our people, clients, communities and the planetWe’re open and seek new and better ways of exceeding expectationsWe’re together and as one team; the whole is greater than the sum of the partsWe’re ambitious and embrace opportunity, to lead essential infrastructure services for lifeWhether you’re a trainee, apprentice or graduate, or progressing through your career, our people benefit from industry recognised programmes, training and development.It’s an exceptional time to be a part of M Group.Please note: Occasionally, job adverts might be closed before the stated closing date. Do apply as soon as possible to ensure your application is considered.For certain roles, successful candidates will be subject to 3rd party background checks as part of the hiring process. Some roles require drug and alcohol testing as part of induction and onboarding.#MGroupW IND2

title: ER Advisor
description:
OverviewPermanent Up to £35,000 + Pension + PMI + ShareSave + 6.6 weeks holiday + Hybrid Working (2 days per week in the office;   4 days per week will be required during induction period)  Southampton, Store Support Office We believe anyone can improve their home to make life better. From our Southampton Store Support office (SSO) we equip our stores, our people, and our whole business with everything it takes to help our millions of customers create a home they’ll love. Join us as an ER Advisor and you’ll be a big part of this. Role Purpose:  To be the conscience of the business, providing professional, consistent advice, support and coaching on all employment relations issues to managers in SSO and Retail. Ensure a fair and consistent approach is applied in relation to company policies and procedures, minimising potential commercial risks. What's the job? Key Accountabilities / Responsibilities Respond to all employment relations queries in line with our policies and agreed SLAs, asking all relevant questions to fully understand the situation and query.  Inspire confidence and encourage the decision maker to make informed decisions by providing expert advice, support and coaching.  Draft relevant letters that are well written, grammatically and factually correct, include everything necessary and minimise risk.  Ensure stakeholders understand the policies, processes, options, advice given and tools available.  Provide effective day-to-day administration in relation to the ER role, including accurately logging calls and responding accurately to emails.  Develop and maintain effective working relationships with all stakeholders.  Proactively contribute to the team by working collaboratively, sharing knowledge, giving feedback and maintaining effective working relationships.  Drive relevant focus areas by updating and training colleagues and making continuous improvements, including simplifying processes and improving efficiency.  Attend internal and external training courses as required and keep up to date with relevant internal and external information.  Provide options and recommendations where relevant and effectively contribute to, and influence where necessary, ad-hoc projects within and outside the team.  Provide face-to-face advice and note-taking support to managers in SSO and, occasionally, Retail.  Maintain and develop supporting tools and materials, including policies and How to Guides.  Case manage complex cases, considering all components and formulating a strategy for a satisfactory resolution. Key Business Relationships Work with line managers to effectively manage all employment relations queries.  Work with in-house Solicitors and the Data Protection team to ensure the legal view and any risks are identified and taken into account.  Work, liaise and communicate with the following teams: Retail and SSO HR, Risk, Fraud, Reward, Payroll and external providers such as Occupational Health and Access to Work. What We NeedRequired Skills & Experience: Previous Experience within Employment Relations  CIPD Level 5 (Desirable)  Sound judgement and risk assessment  Coaching and influencing  Effective questioning and active listening  Clear verbal and written communication  Complex case management and problem-solving  Commercial awareness and pragmatic decision-making  Prioritisation, resilience and attention to detail  What's in it for me?  What's In It For You? At B&Q, we're building more than great homes – we're building great careers.When you join us, you'll be part of a supportive, inclusive business where your ideas matter, your development is invested in, and your wellbeing is genuinely important.Here's What You Can Expect🏡 Flexible & Hybrid Working - Work in a way that helps you perform at your best, balancing business needs with personal commitments.📈 Career Growth & Development - Access learning, development and career opportunities across one of the UK's leading retail organisations.💰 Competitive Reward Package - A competitive salary, pension and a range of financial benefits.🛒 Colleague Discounts - Enjoy discounts across B&Q and the wider Kingfisher Group.❤️ Health & Wellbeing Support - Access wellbeing resources, health support and employee assistance programmes designed to help you thrive.🌴 Time Away From Work - Generous holiday entitlement and family-friendly policies that support life both inside and outside work.🤝 A Place Where You Belong - We're committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, respected and empowered to be themselves.🌍 Make a Difference - The work you do will have a direct impact on our customers, colleagues and business. Eligibility To Work Please note that B&Q does not currently offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK at the time of application and throughout their employment. Accessibility & Disability Confident At B&Q, we're committed to creating an inclusive recruitment experience for everyone.If you require any additional support or reasonable adjustments to help you complete your application or throughout the recruitment process, please let us know.If you would like to be considered under the Disability Confident Scheme , please contact us at recruitment@b-and-q.co.uk. If you meet the minimum criteria for the role, we'll consider your application in line with our Disability Confident commitments.

title: Senior Human Resources Advisor
description:
Be visionaryTeledyne Technologies Incorporated provides enabling technologies for industrial growth markets that require advanced technology and high reliability. These markets include aerospace and defense, factory automation, air and water quality environmental monitoring, electronics design and development, oceanographic research, deepwater oil and gas exploration and production, medical imaging and pharmaceutical research.We are looking for individuals who thrive on making an impact and want the excitement of being on a team that wins.Job DescriptionWe’re looking for a proactive and experienced Senior HR Advisor who is confident operating in a broad, hands-on generalist role and providing high-quality HR advice to managers and employees. You’ll bring strong generalist HR experience, sound knowledge of UK employment law and the confidence to advise on everything from employee relations and recruitment through to organisational change, talent and reward activities. You’ll be comfortable working independently while building strong relationships across the business and supporting multiple sites.The Senior Human Resources Advisor is a generalist and operational role and is responsible for delivering a wide range of consultative and HR support services to the business and its employees.Responsible for providing high quality, consistent HR service across the organization in the areas of responsibility, you will operate as a HR expert, to advise, guide and support colleagues and managers by providing people management and development support across designated business areas.You will be expected to provide high quality and consistent HR support and generalist advice to the business and its employees, taking responsibility for HR support and advise within the employee lifecycle and for delivering a wide range of consultative HR support services.This role supports multiple sites and there will be a requirement to travel within the UK as and when required, but your base will be at Portchester and it is an onsite position.Key Contacts: Site leads, managers, HR Community, Payroll, General Managers and VPs.Main AccountabilitiesThe first point of contact for managers regarding a wide range of HR topics, e.g. Pay and benefit enquiries, company policy questions and day to day queries across the life cycle of employment. Lead on recruitment activities and taking full ownership for recruitment, supporting line managers with recruitment decisions in line with resource planning and internal processes Support people development activities by identifying training needs and working with managers to develop talent and succession plans Provide guidance on people practices such as restructures and succession planning in line with organizational requirements and strategy. Provide accurate and timely generalist HR advice and assistance to support company’s objectives.    Support managers with employee relation matters, in line with company policies and practices. Maintain existing HR related policies and procedures in line with organizational strategy, supporting the wider HR team in discussing and developing revisions/new policies. Work closely with the wider HR team to maintain overall HR engagement and service to stakeholders and customers. Deliver local training on corporate/regional HR matters. Support the wider HR team with HR projects as and when required. Contribute to the continuous improvement of Procedures, Policies and Work Instructions ensuring best practice. Contribute to the HR weekly and monthly metrics reporting for areas of responsibility. Run cyclical HR activities, such as talent reviews, the annual compensation review cycle and salary benchmarking exercise, and the promotions cycle. title: Product Manager
description:
As a trusted partner, our Public Health mission is to make food systems safer, healthier and more sustainable. Throughout our global network in 27 countries, we offer to our customers a wide range of testing and innovative solutions dedicated to preventing health risks related to food, environment and consumer goods. External growth has been a key pillar of our history with more than 40 acquisitions completed in the last 10 years.If you want to contribute to an inspiring long-term purpose, to be part of a fast growing company on a high-value market with significant build-up opportunities, and to grow in an entrepreneurial and warm environment, join us! Northern Europe Cluster Industry Product Manager We are looking for a Northern Europe Cluster Industry Product Manager to support and grow the industry portfolio across the Pharma Quality Control and Food Safety & Quality markets. This role sits at the intersection of science, marketing and business strategy, transforming market insights into commercial actions that drive portfolio growth and customer value across the Northern Europe Cluster.Working closely with local commercial teams, regional stakeholders and global product management teams, the Industry Product Manager will support portfolio performance, market development and customer engagement activities. The role requires a balance of scientific knowledge, commercial awareness and strategic thinking, enabling informed decisions around product positioning, pricing, lifecycle management and business opportunities.Reporting into the Northern Europe Cluster Marketing organisation, the Industry Product Manager will collaborate extensively across Sales, Marketing, Customer Service, Application Specialists and Global Product Management teams. This is a field-based role with regular travel across the Northern Europe Cluster and France, providing direct exposure to customers, laboratories, industry events and key stakeholders.What will your responsibilities be?  Manage the Industry portfolio throughout the product lifecycle, from launch and market introduction through to phase-out and end-of-life activities.  Monitor portfolio performance, identifying growth opportunities and supporting actions to improve business results and market penetration.  Support pricing strategy development and pricing policy recommendations, ensuring alignment with commercial objectives and market conditions.  Contribute to portfolio positioning, value proposition development and deployment of strategic marketing initiatives across the region.  Gather, analyse and interpret market, competitive, customer and regulatory intelligence to support business decisions and commercial strategy.  Monitor industry trends, customer needs and competitor activities, identifying opportunities and risks impacting portfolio performance.  Provide market insights and recommendations to marketing and commercial teams to support business planning and growth initiatives.  Support annual budgeting, forecasting and business review processes, contributing to performance analysis and demand planning activities.  Partner with commercial teams to provide product expertise, technical support and tactical guidance during customer engagements.  Participate in customer visits, laboratory visits and strategic account discussions to better understand market needs and strengthen customer relationships.  Gather customer feedback and communicate market requirements to regional and global product management teams.  Build relationships with industry influencers, key opinion leaders and strategic stakeholders across the pharmaceutical and food sectors.  Support the development and execution of the Marketing Action Plan, ensuring alignment with regional and global objectives.  Contribute to the creation of customer-facing materials, product training content and promotional activities.  Plan, organise and participate in congresses, exhibitions, demonstrations, workshops and user meetings to support awareness and demand generation.  Collaborate effectively across local, regional and global functions to ensure successful execution of portfolio and marketing initiatives. Who are you?  Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in Microbiology, Molecular Biology, Biomedical Science or a related scientific discipline.  Strong understanding of industrial microbiology, quality control processes and laboratory environments within the pharmaceutical, food or related industries.  Experience in product management, marketing, sales, business development or another customer-facing B2B role is advantageous.  Commercially aware, with confidence analysing portfolio performance, pricing strategies, forecasts and business opportunities.  Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate market intelligence and data into actionable recommendations.  Excellent communication and presentation skills, capable of engaging both technical and commercial audiences.  Ability to influence stakeholders and drive collaboration across multiple functions without direct authority.  Customer-focused, proactive and results-oriented, with a strong commitment to delivering business growth and customer value.  Highly organised, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and projects simultaneously.  Proficient in Microsoft Office applications; experience with CRM systems and commercial reporting tools is beneficial.  Fluent in English, with strong written and verbal communication skills.  Willingness to travel extensively (30%+ of working time) across the Northern Europe Cluster and France.  Comfortable working within an international, matrix organisation and collaborating with diverse regional and global stakeholders. Why join us? This role offers the opportunity to work at the intersection of science, marketing and commercial strategy while supporting a diverse portfolio across the pharmaceutical and food industries. You will gain broad exposure to international stakeholders, product lifecycle management, customer engagement activities, strategic marketing initiatives and business development projects, while contributing directly to the growth of bioMérieux's Industry business across the Northern Europe Cluster.

title: Digital Delivery Manager
description:
Job SummaryThe Office for National Statistics (ONS) is the UK’s largest producer of official statistics, covering a range of key economic, social, and demographic topics. These include measuring changes in the value of the UK economy, estimating the size, geographic distribution, and characteristics of the population, and providing indicators of price inflation, employment, earnings, crime, and migration.This role is within the Advanced Data Formats Service in Digital Publishing, which aims to support users to find, understand, explore and use ONS data. We look after and improve the services that make data available through the ONS website, downloads, interactive tools and APIs, while developing better ways for people and machines to access trusted statistics. Our work brings together data, technology and user needs, replacing older services with simpler, more joined-up ways to publish and use ONS data.Job DescriptionA delivery manager will build and maintain teams, ensuring they are motivated, collaborating and working well. The complexity or breadth of products or teams will vary in this role, depending on the context.They Also:Identify obstacles and help the team to overcome them.Focus the team on what is most important to the delivery of products and services. Encourage and facilitate continuous improvement of the delivery team.Coach and mentor both team members and others to apply the most appropriate Agile and Lean tools and techniques. Person specificationEssential Criteria:Agile and Lean Practices (Practitioner):You Can:compare and select the most appropriate delivery methods and processesrecognise, reflect and adapt when something does not work, encouraging experimentationuse a blended approach depending on the contexthelp teams to measure, evaluate and visualise outcomesencourage reflective practice to improve ways of working You Can:Communicating between the technical and non-technical (Practitioner):listen to and interpret the needs of technical and non-technical stakeholders, and manage their expectationsmanage active and reactive communicationsupport or host difficult discussions within the team or with diverse senior stakeholders You Can:Maintaining delivery momentum (Practitioner):Facilitate the delivery flow of a team, managing the pace and tempo.Actively address internal and external risks, issues and dependencies including where ownership exists outside the team. You Can:Making the process work (Expert):Identify and challenge organisational processes of increasing complexity and those processes that are unnecessarily complicated.Add value and can coach the organisation to inspect and adapt processes.Understand external suppliers’ delivery approaches and adapt to ensure interface to ONS delivery approach is smooth, challenging external supplier to align more closely where appropriate.Guide teams through the implementation of a new process. Life cycle management (Working)You Can:manage the delivery of products and services that add value through different phases of the life cycle, with some supportidentify if the product or service should move to the next phase and, if it should, how to do thisensure the product or service is developed in line with the appropriate service standards for a phaseuse new information to adapt approaches to life cycle managementBehavioursWe'll assess you against these behaviours during the selection process:Changing and ImprovingDelivering at PaceWorking TogetherCommunicating and InfluencingBenefitsAlongside your salary of £43,329, Office for National Statistics contributes £12,552 towards you being a member of the Civil Service Defined Benefit Pension scheme.  Find out what benefits a Civil Service Pension provides (opens in a new window).The Office for National Statistics is part of the Civil Service, and as such we share a number of key benefits with other departments, whilst also having our own unique offerings to support our valued colleagues across the organisation.Whether you are hearing about us for the first time or already know a bit about our organisation, we hope that our careers site will give you a great insight into the benefits and facilities available to our colleagues, and our fantastic working culture. Inclusion & AccessibilityAt ONS we are always looking to attract the very best people from the widest possible talent pool, and we are proud to be an inclusive, equal opportunities employer. As a Disability Confident Leader we’re committed to ensuring that all candidates are treated fairly throughout the recruitment process.As part of our application process, you will be prompted to provide details of any reasonable adjustments to our recruitment process that you need. If you would like to discuss any reasonable adjustments before applying, please contact the recruitment team in the first instance.If you would like an accessible version of any of the attachments or recruitment documents below or linked to in this advert, please contact the recruitment team who will be happy to assist.Things you need to knowSelection process detailsThis vacancy is using Success Profiles (opens in a new window), and will assess your Behaviours and Experience.We are dedicated to providing equal opportunities for all, and are proud participants in the following initiatives:Disability Confident Scheme (opens in new window).Great Place to Work for Veterans (opens in a new window).Redeployment Interview Scheme (open to Civil Service employees at risk of redundancy who meet the minimum requirements)Visa SponsorshipONS is unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. This is a unique opportunity to take a leading role in shaping Thames Water’s long-term water resources strategy, helping to ensure a resilient water supply for millions of customers while navigating some of the industry's most complex regulatory and environmental challenges. As our WRMP Strategy and Planning Manager, you’ll lead programme coordination, influence strategic decision-making, and work with senior stakeholders across the business, regulatory bodies, and industry partners to deliver our future Water Resources Management Plans.What you'll be doing as a WRMP Strategy and Planning ManagerAs our WRMP Strategy and Planning Manager, you'll provide leadership across the planning, governance and delivery of Thames Water's Water Resources Management Plan programme, ensuring technical workstreams remain aligned, risks are managed, and regulatory commitments are successfully delivered. You'll be at the heart of strategic planning activities, working across multiple disciplines to drive outcomes that will shape the future of water resources across our region.Lead the coordination and delivery of Water Resources Management Plan activities and associated regulatory submissions.Provide oversight, challenge and assurance across technical planning workstreams, consultants and key stakeholders.Build strong relationships with regulators, regional planning groups and industry partners.Manage programme risks, dependencies and critical milestones to ensure successful delivery.Lead and develop a small team, creating a collaborative and high-performing environment.Drive continuous improvement across planning processes, governance and ways of working.Base location: Clearwater Court, Reading (Hybrid)Working pattern: 36 hours per week, with office attendance typically required on Tuesdays and Thursdays.What you should bring to the roleThe must-haves (essential criteria) for this opportunity include:Demonstrable experience in UK water resources planning and a strong understanding of Water Resources Management Plan requirements and regulatory frameworks.Technical experience in at least one area of Water Resource Management Planning (E.g. Supply Forecasting, Demand forecasting, Demand Management)Experience working within, or closely supporting, a UK water company.Proven ability to lead or coordinate complex technical programmes with multiple stakeholders and competing priorities.Strong stakeholder management skills, with the confidence to engage and influence across all levels of an organisation and external bodies.Line management experience and a passion for developing high-performing teams.Degree qualification in a relevant discipline or equivalent experience.Nice-to-haves that would make you stand out:Experience delivering or supporting statutory Water Resources Management Plans.Experience working with Water Resources South East (WRSE) or similar regional planning organisations.Knowledge of programme management tools such as Microsoft Project or Primavera P6.Experience using AI and emerging technologies to improve planning and programme delivery.Chartered status or working towards chartership in a relevant technical discipline.What's in it for you?This is a rare opportunity to influence one of the largest and most important water resources programmes in the UK. Plan, allocate and supervise engineering work to achieve project objectives and agreed technical outcomes. Promote compliance with applicable engineering processes, governance, safety, security and quality requirements. Demonstrable competence at Senior Engineer level or equivalent.  Desirable Chartered Engineer status, or evidence of actively working towards professional registration.  Relevant project, engineering management or leadership qualification. Essential Skills Strong technical leadership, with the ability to provide direction, coordination and support to engineers working across multiple activities.  Effective planning, prioritisation and organisation of engineering work within delivery constraints.  The ability to assess technical feasibility, challenge assumptions and support sound engineering decisions.  Clear written and verbal communication with technical, project and customer stakeholders.  Confident stakeholder management and the ability to influence across disciplines and organisational boundaries.  A practical approach to managing delivery risk, dependencies, issues and change.  The ability to balance technical integrity with programme, cost and schedule requirements.  Sound judgement, accountability and a collaborative leadership style.  Knowledge of systems and software engineering within complex defence programmes.  Understanding of mission-critical environments.  Familiarity with engineering lifecycle governance, technical reviews, configuration management and assurance.  Coaching, mentoring and capability development of engineers and technicians. Experience Engineering management, technical leadership or work package leadership in a complex engineering environment.  Leading and influencing engineers to deliver defined technical objectives.  Planning and supervising engineering activity, including assignment of work and review of progress.  Managing delivery against agreed scope, schedule, cost, quality and risk expectations.  Working with multi-disciplinary teams and a range of internal and external stakeholders.  Reviewing and resolving complex engineering problems.  UK Defence, maritime, naval or other safety-critical engineering programmes.  Marine training and simulation projects, systems or services.  Management of small projects, services, contracts, departments, suppliers or subcontracted work.  Customer-facing technical delivery in a regulated or secure environment.  Experience coordinating suppliers, subcontractors or externally delivered engineering activity. title: Product Engineering Lead

Job DescriptionYour ImpactDue to growth of the business area, an increasing workload and development within the team, we have a requirement to fill the vacancy of Project Engineering Lead within our Naval Line of Business (LoB), part of the Integrated Sensing and Protection (ISP) division with Leonardo Electronics UK.Within this LoB, the projects are diverse and exciting. There are a large number of projects in various stages of their lifecycle from new core product development, business capture, customer-funded projects and in service support contracts.The Naval business is planning for growth over the next 5 years as part of the Integrated Business Plan. As such, there is requirement to further develop a high performance culture within Naval to realise the growth potential that exists. The Naval business has many technologies deployed across various platforms, and as such are seen as a systems design and integration for our customers, aiding them in finding the best solution for their requirements.With all of this, the opportunity to be involved as a Project Engineering Lead represents a chance to be at the heart of a diverse range of technologies and exciting projects across the full engineering lifecycle.The Project Engineering Lead ensures the delivery of the overall Engineering solution that is compliant with Customer, Contractual, Statutory & Regulatory and Company requirements and that all engineering activities are effectively planned and managed from a performance, schedule and cost perspective. Project Engineering Leads are responsible for the total engineering activity undertaken on a project or portfolio of projects and so manage cross-disciplined engineering teams.Reporting to a Project Engineering Manager, the Project Engineering Lead contributes to the monthly engineering governance cycle through preparation of engineering status reports. Project Engineering Leads build strong relationships with Engineering Functional Leads to ensure company-engineering frameworks and processes are followed. Project Engineering Leads may also have a team of engineers reporting directly to them. Project Engineering Leads play a key role in business winning activities, coordinating the collection of engineering costs, preparation of engineering plans and holding engineering bid reviews.The role requires a candidate who is self-motivated, proactive and enthusiastic, with strong leadership and communication skills. The ability to foster and develop effective working relationships is key to ensure engineers perform to the levels required of the projects. A strong commercial and business awareness is also essential to ensure that the engineering effort can be managed in the correct context for each given project.Key Responsibility Areas Project Engineering Leads are responsible for the management of multi-disciplined engineering teams across multiple projects. Working closely with Project Managers, they are responsible for delivery of the overall engineering output against time, cost and performance budgets.Project Engineering Leads are responsible for generating clear and relevant engineering plans, establishing key milestones and identifying risks, opportunities and interdependencies.Project Engineering Leads are responsible for reviewing the current engineering positions on projects, and adapting plans as required to mitigate risks to either cost, schedule or performance budgets. Project Engineering Leads are responsible for preparation and communication of monthly engineering status reports for each of their assigned projects into their line manager, the Project Engineering Manager.Project Engineering Leads are responsible for the coordination of engineering input into bids as part of the business winning process.This role sits on the multi-functional management team of the Naval business area, representing engineering on that team at weekly and monthly progress and reporting meetings. Skills, Qualifications & Knowledge RequiredThe following skills and experience are required:Educated to a degree level in an engineering-related subject (essential)Previous experience of managing and/or leading multi-disciplined engineering teams (essential)Strong understanding and proven track record of engineering lifecycles and processes (essential)Strong understanding of creation and monitoring of work breakdown structures, engineering plans, risk management and costs (essential)A strong understanding and experience of systems integration and testing (desirable)Experience of working within the defence industry (desirable) Intrinsic FactorsThe candidate must have demonstrable relevant experience and proven success in their previous roles.The candidate must have well-rounded engineering experience in all phases of the design lifecycle, and must have previous exposure to all aspects of engineering planning.This is not an exhaustive list, and we are keen to hear from you even if you might not have experience in all the above. The most important skill is a good attitude and willingness to learn.Security ClearanceThis role is subject to pre-employment screening in line with the UK Government’s Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS). An additional range of Personnel Security Controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV) may apply, this could include meeting the eligibility requirements for The Security Check (SC) or Developed Vetting (DV). For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vettingWhy join usAt Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive.Time to Recharge: Enjoy generous leave with the opportunity to accrue up to 12 additional flexi-days each year.Secure your Future: Benefit from our award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution.Your Wellbeing Matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity (Enable, Pride, Equalise, Armed Forces, Carers, Wellbeing and Ethnicity).Rewarding Performance: All employees at management level and below are eligible for our bonus scheme.Never Stop Learning: Free access to 4,000+ online courses via Coursera and LinkedIn Learning.Refer a friend: Receive a financial reward through our referral programme.Tailored Perks: Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more.Flexible working: Flexible hours with hybrid working options. For part time opportunities, please talk to us about what might be possible for this role.For a full list of our company benefits please visit our website.Leonardo is a global leader in Aerospace, Defence, and Security. Our employees are not just part of a team—they are key contributors to shaping innovation, advancing technology, and enhancing global safety.At Leonardo we are committed to building an inclusive, accessible, and welcoming workplace.
